pr_title: Implement color mode for ZHA light polling to fix color_temp and color_x/y states
pr_body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This fixes color_x/color_y vs color_temp in the polling of ZHA lights.
Zigbee lights still report current_x/current_y and color_temperature even when they can't show both at the same time.
Since the polling of lights in ZHA would add back both color_x/color_y and color_temp to the state in Home Assistant, it now also checks color_mode (like it's done in the native Hue integration in Home Assistant) to determine whether or not color_temp or color_x/color_y should be set.

Try configuring attribute reporting for the "color_mode" and see if all lights would report it. 
Alternatively, after executing a "service call", we could create a task to "read" the color mode attribute, so zigpy would cache it and return `hs_color`, `color_temp` properties based on the cached value of the `color_mode`.
That should alleviate the issue, when you set `color_temp` to None in the service call, but light reports (do they report color temp?) the color temp attribute and it is set again ?

Attribute reports for colors and color temperature aren't parsed at the moment. Only brightness and on/off is correctly parsed and changes the state in Home Assistant afaik. So only the polling of the light will cause the invalid state.
Also, why/how would/could you set ``color_temp`` to None in a service call (using zha.set_zigbee_cluster_attribute)?
I'm not sure if I understood you correctly though.

Hey there @dmulcahey, @adminiuga, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with an integration (`zha`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L534) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
ah, in that case no worries there. I know we do not parse xy_color attributes, but thought we were parsing the color temp attribute

> ah, in that case no worries there. I know we do not parse xy_color attributes, but thought we were parsing the color temp attribute

I'll check again to make sure.
Edit: At least when changing the color (temperature) with the Hue Bluetooth, Home Assistant doesn't update the state until it's polled again.

There's some code here: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/zha/core/channels/lighting.py#L29-L33 but ``attribute_updated`` is only implemented for the LevelControl cluster ``current_level``: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/zha/core/channels/general.py#L215

So these changes seem to be fine (for now), I guess. If/when attribute reports for current_x/current_y and color_temperature are finally parsed, color_mode would also need to be parsed correctly then.

(unrelated note: ZB3 Hue lights send multiple attribute reports during the default 1/10s (or custom) transition time and would also cause the color picker to jump like the brightness slider already does)

You missed the superclass https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2e50c1be8e9594df2c88e1ecb34d7a46d040045c/homeassistant/components/zha/core/channels/base.py#L227

all reported attrs are handled

however there is nothing here: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2e50c1be8e9594df2c88e1ecb34d7a46d040045c/homeassistant/components/zha/light.py#L385  catching those signals...

If this PR is fine, is it possible that it'll still make it into a beta/release of 2021.1? (This is also where the "original" change #44566 will be first implemented.
I'm not sure if users will be confused on why their ZHA lights will revert back to "invalid states" after some time -> when they're polled.)

@TheJulianJES With WS/CT lights can having different max min for the color it can being setted that can being readed from the device (Zigbee standard have one min max but the light can having lesser capacity).
Then setting the color temp of one groupe of light with different min max its dont looks no nice then going outside the range of some of the lights.

Z2M have starting pulling the values and adding the less ones to the groupe so not getting the mismatch of color temperature.

Is it somthing that is interesting for ZHA to implanting ??

issue_context.title: Lights connected via ZHA report both color and color temperature
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Lights connected to ZHA that support both adjustable color_temperature and full RGB colors report their state incorrectly. Steps to reproduce:

1. Reboot Home Assistant and turn ZHA-connected light on. 
2. The light will now report the correct color_temp in its state, and have rgb_color set to [255,255,255]
3. Set RGB color for the light, for example [255,0,0]. The rgb_color in the state will be reported correctly
4. Set the color_temp, for example to 400. 
5. The physical light will change to white light with the correct color temperature, and the color_temp will also be reported correctly in Home Assistant, but the rgb_color will still show up as [255,0,0], resulting in an incorrect color of the light in Lovelace cards

Other integrations remove the rgb_color from the state when color_temp is set, and vice versa remove the color_temp value from the state when an RGB color is set. Without doing so both automations and Lovelace are unable to determine what color the light is set to.  

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.111.4
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): unknown
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Supervised
- Integration causing this issue: ZHA
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/zha/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
n/a (ZHA configured through integrations setup page in web UI)
```
